# How to Use Gemini to Make Your LinkedIn Photo Look Professional at Home

> **In short:** You can ask Gemini to give a snapshot a cleaner, more professional look, as long as you start with a clear, face-forward photo. Image editing may not be available in every country or app version, and the result should still look like you. Check every edit before you post it.

You will learn how to take a good starting photo at home, ask Gemini for a simple professional edit, and check that the result still looks like you. This is for anyone who wants a tidier profile picture without booking a photo session. The steps below are written for a complete beginner.

## Before you start

- **A Google account** and the **Gemini app or the Gemini website** on your phone or computer. Sign in with your Google account when prompted.
- **One clear photo of yourself**, taken in good light. Most people find that a recent photo works best, because LinkedIn viewers are used to seeing your current face.
- **About 20 to 30 minutes.** Image edits can take a minute each, and you may want to try two or three versions.

Image editing is not guaranteed on every plan or in every region. If you can't find an option to upload a picture, it may not be available to you yet.

## Step 1 — Take or choose a clear, face-forward photo

Pick a photo where your whole face is visible, you are looking toward the camera, and the lighting is soft. Stand facing a window during the day so the light falls on your face evenly. Avoid harsh overhead lights and strong backlight, which turns you into a dark silhouette.

Keep the background simple, such as a plain wall. Make sure no one else is in the frame. Shoulders and head should fill most of the picture, and the image should be sharp, not blurry.

If you have to take a new photo, use the back camera of your phone and ask someone to hold it at eye level. If your phone is the only option, set the picture to the highest quality it offers.

You'll know it worked when you can see your eyes, your full face and your shoulders clearly on your screen, with no heavy shadows across your face.

## Step 2 — Open Gemini and find the upload option

Open the Gemini app or website and sign in. Look for a **plus sign, a paperclip, or an image icon** near the text box at the bottom of the screen. Tapping it usually lets you add a photo from your device. The exact icon may vary depending on your phone, browser, or app version, so look around the text box before you give up.

If you don't see any upload option, try the website in a desktop browser, or update the app from your app store. If it still isn't there, your account or region may not have image editing yet. In that case, you can still use the honest tips in Step 6 with a different editing tool.

Once you tap the icon, your device's photo gallery or file browser should open. Choose the photo you picked in Step 1.

You'll know it worked when your selected photo appears as a small preview above or beside the text box.

## Step 3 — Ask Gemini for a simple professional edit

With your photo attached, type a clear instruction in the text box, then send it. Keep the request modest: you want a cleaner look, not a new face. Describe what you want in plain words.

💬 Example: "Make this headshot look more professional with softer, even lighting and a plain light gray background. Keep my face, hairstyle, and expression exactly as they are."

Tapping send usually starts the process, and Gemini shows a loading indicator or message while it works. The reply may come back as a new image, or as text describing a change. If Gemini only describes the edit and doesn't return a picture, ask it directly to create the edited image.

If the result looks different from what you asked for, rephrase with more detail, such as "Keep the same crop and only soften the shadows." Expect to try two or three versions. Gemini may not get it right on the first attempt.

You'll know it worked when Gemini returns an image that looks like a cleaner version of your original photo.

## Step 4 — Compare the edit with your original

Look at the new image and your original side by side, ideally on the same screen. Check your face first: do your eyes, nose, mouth and smile look like yours? Next, check your skin tone, hair and clothing. Gemini should not change your age, build, or features, and it should not add accessories or details you don't wear.

Make sure the background looks natural and that no part of your hair, ears, or shoulders has been blurred or distorted. Zoom in on the edges of your face and on your hands if they're visible.

If the edit changed your face, reject it and try again with a stronger request, such as "Do not change my facial features, only adjust lighting and background." If the result looks too smooth or unnatural, ask for less retouching.

You'll know it worked when someone who knows you would recognize you immediately in the new picture.

## Step 5 — Ask for one small adjustment

If the edit is close but not quite right, ask for one change at a time. Changing several things in one message makes it harder to see which change caused a problem. Keep your follow-up short and specific.

💬 Example: "Keep everything the same, but make the background a little warmer and lighten the shadows under my chin."

Send the message and wait for the new image. Compare it with the previous version, as you did in Step 4. If one change improved the photo and another made it worse, you can ask for only the good change again.

Note that AI tools can make mistakes, such as slightly warping a line or adding an odd shadow. Do not keep asking for edits forever. Usually one or two small adjustments are enough. If you're still unhappy after three rounds, return to your original photo, or try retaking the picture in better light.

You'll know it worked when the image looks clean and you feel comfortable with how it represents you.

## Step 6 — Save the picture and check it before you upload

When you're happy with the result, save the image. Press and hold the image on a phone, or right-click it on a computer, and choose the option that saves or downloads it. You can also use the download or share icon if one appears near the picture. Choose a clear file name, such as "linkedin-headshot-final."

Before you upload it to LinkedIn, view the file at a small size, as a profile picture will appear on a phone. Make sure your face is still easy to see at that size. Then open LinkedIn, go to your profile, and use the edit option for your photo to upload the file. LinkedIn may have its own guidance on profile photos, so check it there.

Finally, ask yourself whether the photo looks like you on a good day. If it doesn't, your original photo is a perfectly good choice too.

You'll know it worked when your new profile photo appears on your LinkedIn profile and still looks like you in the small preview.

## Common mistakes

- **Asking for a new face or body.** Requests like "make me look ten years younger" can change your appearance in ways you didn't intend. Fix it by asking only for lighting, background, or cropping changes, and say you want your features kept the same.
- **Starting with a dark, blurry or cropped photo.** AI edits can't fully repair poor source images. Fix it by retaking the photo in soft daylight, with the camera at eye level.
- **Posting the first result without checking it.** A small change, like a distorted ear or an odd shadow, is easy to miss on a large screen. Fix it by comparing the edit with your original at the same size, as in Step 4.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** A good profile picture can be a simple, low-cost way to refresh your photo for social media, a community group, or a club directory.
- **For your business or work:** If you're updating a professional profile, a clean, natural-looking headshot helps people recognize you when you meet them in person or on a video call.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a photo you already took in good daylight, then make one small request. Small steps are easier to check.

## Try it now

Open Gemini, attach your best face-forward photo, and send this message: "Keep my face, hairstyle, and expression exactly as they are, and make the lighting softer and even." Compare the result with your original, and you'll have a first version in about two minutes.
